text:
jess_cs: Heads up — onboarding call with Nimbus. Android client getting 403s immediately after we rotate keys, iOS + web fine.

owen_eng: any error text? stack trace?

jess_cs: paste from their device logs: 
```
W/HttpClient: request failed: 403 Forbidden
body: {
  "error": "invalid_api_key"
}
endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate tenant=nimbus-prod
headers: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (rotated)
```

lina_infra: Do they use a mobile proxy / CDN? Android often reuses connections and some proxies cache auth responses.

jess_cs: They route mobile traffic through CloudFront -> internal API gateway. They said they don't cache, but config might be default.

harry_support: Quick triage steps we asked them to run: 1) call /v1/init after rotation and log the token they get, 2) send curl from laptop to same gateway to compare, 3) confirm Android SDK isn't holding token in SharedPreferences after refresh.

owen_eng: Also check HTTP/2 connection reuse. If client keeps connection open and backend rotates key, a connection-level auth might be cached by edge. We can add a server-side guard: accept the previous key for a short window.

jess_cs: customer ran curl and got 200 with new token. Android app still 403. They captured a packet trace showing Authorization header with new token — but the edge returns cached 403 from origin earlier.

lina_infra: Two immediate fixes: 1) set Cache-Control: no-store / no-cache on auth and token exchange endpoints; 2) ensure CloudFront forwards Authorization header and sets minimum TTL=0 for those paths. I'll add a note to the onboarding checklist.

owen_eng: I'll enable "previous_key_accept_seconds=180" for tenant nimbus-prod for the rotation window so we don't force a CDN flush. Also will emit a debug metric for rotation rejections so we can monitor.

harry_support: For customers: we should add a small SDK note: after key rotate, call /v1/init and then do a short exponential backoff for generate (so transient 403s don't fail UX) and avoid caching tokens to disk until confirmed.

jess_cs: Nimbus confirms Android 2.4.1 uses token caching in app startup path. We've asked them to change to ephemeral in-memory until verified. They've rolled that change to a canary — will report.

lina_infra: Done: CloudFront behavior updated to forward Authorization, TTL=0 on /v1/init and /v1/auth. Onboarding doc updated: "Mobile + CDN: forward Authorization, TTL=0, and prefer no-store on auth responses."

owen_eng: previous_key_accept_seconds toggled=180 for tenant=nimbus-prod. Watch logs/metrics for rotation_reject_count.

jess_cs: Canary reports success. Android canary now gets 200s after rotation. We'll keep previous_key_accept_seconds for 24h then revert to 0.

harry_support: Action items: 1) add FAQ entry about rotation and CDNs, 2) patch Android SDK docs about token caching pattern, 3) ops to revert tenant toggle in 24h.

ops-bot: Thread archived automatically after 7 days of inactivity.
